summary: Kit content tools separates runtime tools from terminal slash commands. Its lifecycle connects six canonical capability bundles through pure previews, one four-domain discovery catalog, complete draft evidence, guarded-mode semantic review, documentation query, whole-piece reads, and bounded result handles. Nine direct tools begin each turn. Search may reveal up to five deferred schemas, collapsed browse reveals none, and exact describe reveals one. Studio lifecycle contains typed creation for character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and media pack without an existing target. Selected JSON Schemas carry field descriptions, defaults, and media reference rules. Normal pieces up to 64,000 characters return in one read. Guarded mode hands apply to the application's review card; autopilot may auto-allow caution writes and full-auto may auto-allow access above the safety floor. Atomic create-only apply refuses occupied IDs and verifies storage. Repeated identical reads stop early. docs_query supplies bounded traversal. Unit and integration proof exists; live terminal verification remains required.

sections.title: Built lifecycle
sections.summary: Built lifecycle connects six canonical capability bundles to Kit. entities capabilities owns IDs, provider names, search, collapsed navigation, exposure, and the descriptor contract. kit capabilities adapts content and non-content descriptors into one unique-name registry. capability_find accepts inferred actions and flat kinds. Six studio lifecycle tools create character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, or media-pack drafts without existing targets or writes. Each has exact-name draft safety. Selected schemas describe required fields, defaults, and media reference conventions only after discovery. kit changes retains baseline, escrow, warnings, platform impact, and create or update mode. Review remains application-owned. Update apply compares revisions; create apply atomically refuses occupied IDs; both verify. studio_read returns one normal whole piece, result_query handles genuinely oversized observations, and nearby identical reads stop early. Tool-budget and cancellation exits preserve provider tool-call/result pairing without running cancelled mutations. docs_query remains catalog-only. Reads overlap while mutations serialize. /tools is the target-aware Panel Deck. Backstage owns lifecycle receipts.

sections.title: Capability contract
sections.summary: A content capability is a pure semantic operation declaring a stable dotted ID, kind, navigation metadata, platform applicability, Zod input, effect, exposure, concurrency key, and preview. Preview returns a complete canonical entity, changes, warnings, platform impact, and optionally a deterministic read observation. It never writes. The composer rejects identity or original escrow changes. The read adapter also requires a canonically identical entity and empty changes, preventing analysis from creating a mutation draft.

sections.title: Apply and authorization
sections.summary: The safety subsystem owns exact-name access classification and never trusts prefixes, discovery metadata, or a claimed runtime effect. Pure content capabilities derive read or preview-only draft access from validated catalog metadata. Each of the six creation workflows has a separate safety-owned exact-name draft classification. Guarded apply pauses in an application-owned semantic review card. Update apply compares the expected revision under a per-path lock. Create apply uses a distinct atomic create-only operation that refuses an occupied ID rather than overwriting or minting a sibling. Stale state and collisions write nothing. Both modes re-read and verify canonical fields and non-Studio escrow. Unreadable or mismatched verification reports failure without retry.

sections.title: Progressive exposure
sections.summary: The unique-name registry remains dispatchable while each turn starts with nine direct tools. One discovery catalog serves content, studio, transfer, and diagnostics. Deferred entries include content capabilities and six studio creation workflows. capability_find infers search from query, describe from ID, and browse otherwise; it accepts a flat kind and content-kind area shorthand. Search reveals at most five matches, browse returns collapsed metadata, and describe reveals one typed operation. The next provider snapshot receives only selected schemas. Creation schemas document lore entries, persona brief versus content, preset blocks and media flags, sealed regex rules, and portrait or pack refs with MIME guidance. Hidden descriptors never surface. studio_read returns normal pieces up to 64,000 characters in one observation; oversized pieces use handles and traversal. Repeated identical reads stop early. Draft query validates current revision or create-time absence without writing.

children.title: Canonical reads and result handles
children.summary: studio_read defaults to one complete canonical entity. A normal piece up to 64,000 characters returns inline in one observation, avoiding forced section traversal. It can still outline immediate children as RFC 6901 JSON Pointers or read one selected value with offsets and limits. Invalid pointers fail closed. Larger whole pieces enter a session-local store and return an opaque result-N handle plus a 4,096-character peek. Other result-producing tools retain the shared 4,096-character inline threshold. result_query provides stat, bounded read, and literal case-insensitive search. Handles reveal no path and expire with the session. Storage caps are 24 entries, 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes per entry, and 4,000,000 UTF-8 bytes total with oldest-first eviction. Content beyond the store cap remains recoverable through direct studio_read offsets.

children.title: Complete draft review
children.summary: Every composed operation retains validated input, changes, warnings, and platform impact, while the draft aggregates warning and impact evidence over one immutable baseline. change_query list returns compact state and counts. show returns operations, baseline, complete proposed entity, warnings, and platform impact, using a result handle or explicit offsets for large proposals. validate re-parses canonical shape and compares the live stored revision without mutating draft state or writing. Per-operation rollback remains excluded until deterministic replay is specified.

sections.title: Character slice
sections.summary: studio.character.create needs no existing target. It accepts a safe optional ID or derives one, then builds a canonical character from identity, persona, scenario, greeting, examples, tags, portrait, and additional media. Portrait and media schemas describe data URI, HTTP(S), and existing asset references, MIME types, roles, labels, and primary selection. It returns structured application-Gate review and uses atomic create-only verified apply. Existing characters retain ten preview-only capabilities covering identity, prompts, greetings, metadata, presentation, media, links, variants, settings, and embedded behavior scripts. Script payloads remain sealed data and original escrow remains non-editable.

sections.title: Lorebook slice
sections.summary: studio.lorebook.create builds a new book and optionally typed initial entries with content, literal or regex triggers, selective logic, insertion position, depth, role, and defaults for the remaining canonical activation fields. Existing drop-ins are settings.update, entries.update, entries.reorder, entries.enable, and entries.remove. Duplicate, separate entry-create, trigger-specific update, placement-specific update, and broad bulk operations remain future additions. The Web UI retains local selection, focus, generated-ID, and undo behavior.

sections.title: Other canonical bundles
sections.summary: Persona creation separates shelf brief from injected content and accepts sections, traits, identity, rating, and portrait. Preset creation accepts prompt blocks, sampler values, and media-inlining settings. Regex creation accepts stored rules with patterns, flags, replacements, phases, depth bounds, and ordering but never executes them. Pack creation accepts expression items with IDs, labels, refs, MIME types, enabled state, and default label. Existing capabilities continue editing each kind through shared entity reducers.

sections.title: Hoplight documentation query
sections.summary: docs_query is a direct read-only meta-tool with four actions. browse lists collections and pages from index metadata only, with root or immediate children, limit 12 cap 25, offset pagination, and slash-separated collection ids that never path-escape. outline returns a semantic page overview and collapsed H2 map without loading Markdown; a returned section slug expands only that branch and its H3 summaries. search ranks body text plus title, short summary, semantic summary, topics, and headings with in-memory BM25. read alone returns authoritative source prose: omit the section for a whole document or select a slug for a targeted nugget. Bounded responses provide continuation offsets so long documents can be read completely across calls. Whole-document reads are preferred around located answers to preserve qualifications, failure conditions, and current-versus-planned distinctions. Semantic navigation merges only from docs/summaries sidecars with current independent APPROVE receipts bound to source and semantic-summary hashes. Authoring discovery is folder-derived from docs/. New and edited pages require authoring, stamping, focused checking, and independent review. Global check requires every page APPROVED. No embeddings or network.

sections.title: Verification status
sections.summary: Proof covers compact discovery, all six creation descriptors and previews, selected-schema media guidance, exact-name draft safety, duplicate-name refusal, whole-card reads through 64,000 characters, oversized storage, repeated-read stopping, JSON Pointer traversal, and complete draft evidence. Creation proof includes no preview writes, canonical create mode, atomic create-only persistence, occupied-ID refusal, one-shot apply, and verification. Update proof retains composition, escrow preservation, stale refusal, one-save apply, and a fake-provider rename journey. Live terminal verification remains required.
